EditingNot permitted - photo must be unaltered by software
Governing bodyHome Office / UK Visas and Immigration, using HMPO photo standards

Photo Size: Printed and Digital

For a paper application, your printed photo must measure exactly 35mm wide by 45mm tall. Within that frame, the distance from the crown of your head to your chin must fall between 29mm and 34mm. GOV.UK notes this is the same size produced by standard UK photo booths, and warns that a photo cropped down from a larger picture will not be accepted.

For an online application, you upload a digital photo instead. GOV.UK does not publish a DPI figure for this file. Instead, the digital photo must be:

  • At least 600 pixels wide and 750 pixels tall
  • Between 50KB and 10MB in size
  • Clear, in focus, in colour, and unaltered by computer software

Background Colour: Cream or Light Grey

This is where applicants most often go wrong. For printed photos, GOV.UK requires a plain cream or light grey background, in clear contrast to your clothing and features. A pure white background is not one of the two approved options, so it is safer to use grey or cream rather than white.

For a digital photo taken during an online application, GOV.UK's wording is broader: the background must simply be plain and light-coloured, in clear contrast to you. In both cases, the background must have no other objects, no other people, no patterns, and no shadows.

Face and Expression

GOV.UK sets the following rules for how you must appear in the photo:

  • Face forwards and look straight at the camera
  • Keep a plain expression with your mouth closed
  • Keep both eyes open and clearly visible
  • Do not let hair fall in front of your eyes
  • Do not wear a head covering, unless it is for religious or medical reasons
  • Do not let anything cover your face
  • Avoid any shadows on your face or on the background
  • Avoid 'red eye'

Glasses: Allowed Only If You Need Them

GOV.UK's rule is more nuanced than many guides suggest: you should not wear glasses in your photo unless you have to. If you do need to wear them, they cannot be sunglasses or tinted glasses, and your eyes must not be covered by the frames or by any glare, reflection, or shadow. Contact lenses avoid this issue entirely, since they are not visible in the photo.

Headwear

GOV.UK does not permit head coverings in visa or passport photos, with one exception: coverings worn for religious or medical reasons are allowed. The same rules on shadows and visibility still apply, so make sure lighting does not cast a shadow across your face from the covering.

Printed Photo Requirements

If you apply using a paper form, you need 2 identical photographs. According to GOV.UK, they must be:

  • Printed to a professional standard, clear and in focus
  • In colour, on plain white photographic paper with no border
  • Free of creases or tears
  • Unmarked on both sides, unless a photo needs to be countersigned
  • Unaltered by computer software
  • Separated from each other and left loose, not attached to your application form

Does This Apply to Every UK Visa Category?

Yes. UK Visas and Immigration applies the same 35x45mm photo specification across visa routes, including the Standard Visitor Visa, Student Visa, Skilled Worker Visa, Family Visa, Graduate Visa, and Indefinite Leave to Remain. Whether you apply online or by paper form determines whether you need a digital file or 2 printed copies, not which size or background rules apply.

Photos of Babies and Children

GOV.UK relaxes some rules for younger applicants:

  • Children must appear alone in the photo, with no toys or dummies for babies
  • Children under 6 do not need to look directly at the camera or hold a plain expression
  • Children under 1 do not need their eyes open; a hand can support their head as long as the hand is not visible in the photo
  • Babies under 1 should lie on a plain, light-coloured sheet, photographed from above

Common Reasons UK Visa Photos Are Rejected

Rejection Reason How to Fix It
Pure white or coloured backgroundUse a plain cream or light grey background for printed photos
Glare, reflection, or shadow from glassesRemove glasses if you can, or adjust lighting so your eyes are fully visible
Head too large or too smallKeep crown-to-chin height between 29mm and 34mm within the 45mm frame
Shadows on the face or backgroundUse even lighting from both sides, not a single overhead source
Smiling or open mouthHold a plain expression with your mouth closed
Hair covering the eyesTie hair back or move it away from your face
Photo older than one monthTake a new photo; GOV.UK enforces this recency rule strictly
Blurry or out-of-focus imageUse a steady camera or tripod and check focus before printing
Digital photo below 600x750 pixelsCheck your camera's output resolution before uploading
Edited or filtered photoSubmit the original, unaltered image

How to Take a Compliant Photo at Home

  1. Choose your background. Stand in front of a plain, light-coloured wall. For a printed photo, cream or light grey works best; avoid a stark white wall.
  2. Set up even lighting. Face a window with natural daylight, or use two lamps positioned at equal distances on either side, so no shadow falls on your face or the background.
  3. Remove glasses if you can. If you must wear them, make sure there is no glare, reflection, or frame shadow over your eyes, and never wear sunglasses or tinted lenses.
  4. Remove headwear, unless you wear it for religious or medical reasons.
  5. Position the camera at eye level, about an arm's length away, and use the main camera rather than a wide-angle selfie lens where possible.
  6. Hold a plain expression. Look straight at the camera, keep your mouth closed, and keep both eyes open and visible.
  7. Check the framing. Your full face, the top of your head, and your shoulders should all be visible, with your head height falling between 29mm and 34mm once printed at 35x45mm.

If you use your own device during an online application, GOV.UK notes that photos from a booth or shop are more likely to be approved than a photo taken on your own device, and that your photo does not need to be pre-cropped since this is done for you.

UK Visa Photo vs UK Passport Photo

Requirement UK Visa UK Passport
Printed photo size35 x 45mm35 x 45mm
Printed backgroundCream or light greyCream or light grey
Head height29-34mm29-34mm
RecencyWithin 1 monthWithin 1 month
Governing bodyHome Office (UKVI)HMPO
Same photo usable for both?Yes, if it meets the specification above for both applications

A Note on Reusing Photos

Since UK visa and passport photos follow the same GOV.UK specification, one compliant photo will generally work for both. Always re-check it against the current rules on gov.uk before each application, in case guidance has changed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I wear glasses in my UK visa photo?

Only if you need them. GOV.UK advises against wearing glasses unless necessary. If you do wear them, they cannot be sunglasses or tinted, and your eyes must be fully visible with no glare, reflection, or shadow from the frames.

Does the background have to be white?

No. For printed photos, GOV.UK requires a plain cream or light grey background, not white. For digital photos taken during an online application, the rule is a plain, light-coloured background.

How old can my UK visa photo be?

It must have been taken within the last month. GOV.UK states clearly that your application will be delayed if your photo does not meet the rules, including this recency requirement.

How many photos do I need for a paper application?

You need 2 identical photographs, left loose and not attached to your form. Online applications use a single digital upload instead.

Can I use my passport photo for my visa application?

Yes, since both follow the same GOV.UK specification, provided the photo still meets the recency rule and every other requirement for the application you are submitting.

Can I wear a hijab, turban, or other religious head covering?

Yes. GOV.UK permits head coverings worn for religious or medical reasons. The same rules on shadows and clear visibility of your face still apply.

What is the minimum digital photo size?

At least 600 pixels wide by 750 pixels tall, between 50KB and 10MB in file size. GOV.UK does not publish a DPI requirement for this file.

Can I take my UK visa photo on my phone?

Yes, though GOV.UK notes that a photo from a booth or shop is more likely to be approved than one taken on your own device. If you do use a phone, keep the lighting even, use a plain light-coloured background, and check the image is in sharp focus before you submit it.

content:
UK Digital Passport Photo: How to Take and Submit One Online (2026)

If you're renewing or applying for a British passport through the gov.uk online service, you need a digital photo rather than a printed one. HM Passport Office (HMPO) only accepts digital images for online applications, and that file has to clear a set of technical and presentation checks before your application can move forward. This guide sets out exactly what those checks are, using the figures gov.uk publishes rather than the DPI conversions that many other sites repeat by mistake.

What a UK Digital Passport Photo Actually Is

A UK digital passport photo is the image file you upload when you apply or renew online through gov.uk. It is a different product from the printed 45mm by 35mm photo used on paper applications. There is no millimetre measurement to hit, because the system crops and scales the photo for you. What matters instead is the pixel size, the file size, and how you appear in the shot, all of which HM Passport Office sets out on its official guidance.

The Official Requirements

Gov.uk states that a digital photo submitted with an online passport application must be:

  • At least 600 pixels wide and 750 pixels tall
  • Between 50KB and 10MB in file size
  • Clear, in focus, and in colour
  • Unaltered by computer software or filters
  • Taken within the last month, even if your appearance hasn't changed
  • Shot against a plain, light-coloured background with clear contrast between you and that background
  • Free of red eye, shadows on your face or behind you, and any other people or objects in the frame

A word of caution here, since it trips up a lot of guides: 413 x 531 pixels is not the government's digital minimum. That number comes from converting the printed 35 x 45mm size at 300 DPI, which is a print calculation, not an upload rule. The figure gov.uk actually asks for online is 600 x 750 pixels, and using a smaller image risks a rejection you didn't need to have.

Beyond the technical checks, gov.uk also sets rules for how you appear. Face forward and look straight at the camera. Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed, and keep both eyes open and clearly visible, with no hair falling across them. Head coverings are not allowed unless worn for religious or medical reasons. Glasses are best left off; if you need them, the lenses must be clear, with no glare, reflection, or frame shadow over your eyes.

Official HMPO digital photo example. Source: gov.uk

Digital Photo vs Printed Photo

Applying online and applying by post lead to two different photo formats. The table below lines them up so you can see exactly where they differ.

Feature Digital Photo (Online) Printed Photo (Paper Form)
Minimum size 600 x 750 px 45mm tall x 35mm wide
File rules Colour image, 50KB to 10MB Plain white photographic paper, no border, no creases
Head height Cropped automatically by the system 29mm to 34mm, crown to chin
Background Plain, light-coloured Plain cream or light grey
Quantity needed 1 digital upload 2 identical prints

Taking Your Own Photo at Home

You do not need a studio to get a compliant photo. You can take it yourself on a phone or camera during the application, though gov.uk notes that photos from a booth or shop are more likely to be approved than ones taken on your own device. If you decide to do it yourself, a few things make the difference between a photo that passes first time and one that gets sent back:

  • Stand facing a plain, light-coloured wall, in even natural light. Avoid harsh overhead lighting, which casts shadows under the eyes and chin.
  • Ask someone else to take the photo for you. HMPO expects self-submitted digital photos to be taken by another person, not as a selfie.
  • Frame your head, shoulders, and upper body in the shot. Do not pre-crop the image yourself; the system does this automatically once you upload it.
  • Remove hats, scarves, and headphones unless you wear them for religious or medical reasons.
  • Keep a neutral expression, with your mouth closed and both eyes open and visible.

HMPO framing guidance for head, shoulders, and upper body. Source: gov.uk

Two Ways to Get Your Digital Photo

Gov.uk gives you two routes into the online application, depending on how you'd rather work.

Get a Photo Code From a Booth or Shop

Before you start your application, visit a photo booth or shop and ask for the option that gives you a code along with your prints. You then enter that code during the online application, and the digital photo linked to it is added to your file automatically. This is the route gov.uk suggests if you want the highest chance of first-time approval.

Upload a Photo From Your Own Device

If you would rather skip the shop, you can take and upload a photo directly during the application. Gov.uk's online service runs an automated check on the image as part of the application itself, flagging anything that falls outside the rules above so you can retake it before you submit.

Photos for Babies and Young Children

Gov.uk relaxes a few rules for younger applicants, since it's rarely practical to get a baby to hold a neutral expression on command:

  • Children must be photographed alone, with no toys or dummies in shot.
  • Children under 6 don't need to look directly at the camera or hold a plain expression.
  • Babies under 1 don't need their eyes open. A hand can support their head, as long as the hand itself is out of frame.
  • Babies under 1 should lie on a plain, light-coloured sheet, photographed from above.

Official HMPO digital photo example for children. Source: gov.uk

Why Digital Photos Get Rejected

Most rejected digital photos fail for one of a handful of reasons, and nearly all of them are avoidable once you know to look for them:

  • The image falls below the 600 x 750 pixel minimum, or has been compressed so heavily that detail is lost.
  • The background isn't plain or light-coloured; patterned, dark, or cluttered backgrounds all fail.
  • Shadows fall across the face or appear behind the subject.
  • Glasses cause glare or reflection, or the frames cover part of the eyes.
  • The expression isn't neutral; smiling or an open mouth are both common culprits.
  • The photo is older than one month.
  • A head covering appears without a religious or medical reason behind it.

Getting the File Right Before You Upload

Most modern phone cameras produce images well above 600 x 750 pixels by default, so the pixel minimum rarely trips people up. The file size band of 50KB to 10MB causes more confusion, mainly because phones now default to formats and compression settings that can push a single photo close to that upper limit, or occasionally under the lower one if heavy compression is applied. Before you upload, check the file's properties on your phone or computer rather than guessing. If your image comes out too large, exporting it again at a slightly lower quality setting, rather than resizing the dimensions, keeps you within the 600 x 750 pixel minimum while bringing the file size down.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use a selfie for my UK digital passport photo?

Yes. Gov.uk allows photos taken on your own device during the application, though it notes that photos from a booth or shop are more likely to be approved on the first attempt.

What is the minimum pixel size for a UK digital passport photo?

At least 600 pixels wide by 750 pixels tall, saved between 50KB and 10MB. Don't rely on the 413 x 531 figure quoted on some sites; that's a print-DPI calculation, not the government's actual digital minimum.

Do I need to crop the photo myself before uploading?

No. Include your head, shoulders, and upper body in the shot, and gov.uk's system handles the cropping for you once it's uploaded.

How recent does the photo need to be?

It must have been taken within the last month, even if your appearance hasn't changed since your last passport.

Can I wear glasses in my digital passport photo?

Only if you need them. If you do, they can't be sunglasses or tinted lenses, and your eyes must be visible without any glare, reflection, or frame shadow.
